items.title: Lillian De Pass Interview, 1960-06-20
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah. But didn't Byron make these first games with the Zuzu? [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, yeah. I hope to tell you. He played good with that.

ctx.x: Well, he started, uh, he told me he used to take two sticks, you know, drumsticks. And his mother had one of them wooden bits. And that's how he started beating drums on the back of the bed. And he used to say, I know, put them sticks down. His mother would get after him by putting the sticks down. And that's how he started playing drums. Beating on the back of his mother's bed. And then after that, well, when he started out with the drums, then he got the drums. That's when he was working with Parker Davis, when…
Yeah. But didn't Byron make these first games with the Zuzu?

Oh, yeah. I hope to tell you. He played good with that. He played good with that. He could play that good. And your Uncle Rudolph went out to play. Your Uncle Rudolph had a little wooden box he made him, about a big like that, covered up with black, uh, with black calico and tack all around with brass, uh, tacks. And he got a little bit of, like a little Christmas horn, and went out and played big job for that. The people clap him and ask him back. What was his name? My, uh, brother-in-law, uh, that's my…
